sections.html:
Manchester Township sellers skew older: nearly half the population, 48.1 percent, is past 65, and the average household has only 1.92 people. That mix points to retirees moving closer to family, heirs settling an estate, and owners who no longer want to maintain a house.

The township in Ocean County had an estimated 46,556 people in mid-2025. Owners occupy 86.7 percent of the housing, the middle home value is $219,100, and tenants pay $1,477 at the median (2020 to 2024 survey). Median household income was $56,885. A quick, as-is sale is a practical option for some owners, especially when a house needs work that a retiree or an estate does not want to fund.

Manchester Township is a wide, mostly wooded township of 81.42 square miles of land, so a sale here depends heavily on which neighborhood the house is in. Lakehurst Naval Air Station lies within its borders, and the borough of Lakehurst is completely surrounded by the township.

Several age-restricted and planned communities sit inside the township, including Pine Lake Park, Crestwood Village, Leisure Village West, Pine Ridge at Crestwood, Leisure Knoll, Cedar Glen Lakes and Cedar Glen West. Whiting is the largest section by area and population, with 33,180 of the township's 45,115 residents in 2020. When the house belongs to a planned community, ask the association for its resale package and any rules on who may buy before listing, since those can add weeks.

Manchester Township requires a Certificate of Re-occupancy for a resale, applied for through the Building Department's online citizen portal. The owner creates a login, chooses the non-rental application, notes whether the house is vacant or occupied (a lockbox or combination can be left for the inspector), submits, and pays the fee online by check or card. The township then emails or calls to schedule the inspection.

The inspection list covers a good deal of the house:

  • Water, electric and gas on, with heating and plumbing in working order.
  • Smoke detectors on every level and within 10 feet of sleeping areas, less than 10 years old, at least 3 feet from vents.
  • Carbon monoxide detectors within 10 feet of bedrooms but not inside them.
  • GFCI outlets that trip on the test button, and covers on every electrical box.
  • House numbers at least 4 inches high, visible from the street.
  • A warning label within 18 inches of the electric panel and meter if solar, a generator or battery storage supplies a second source of power.
  • Open permits closed out, and any unpermitted work cited as a violation.

Houses on well water need a water analysis certification from the Ocean County Health Department. Since April 15, 2025, the state fire code also calls for 18 inches between mulch and combustible parts of a building such as decks and porches.

Steps from contract to recorded deed in Manchester Township
StepWho handles itWhat to expect
Re-occupancy inspectionTownship Building DepartmentOnline application, fee paid online, inspector schedules a visit
Well water analysisOcean County Health DepartmentCertification needed when the house has a private well
Seller residency formNJ Division of TaxationGIT/REP form signed by the person signing the deed, submitted at closing
Realty transfer feeSeller, paid at recordingBased on the price recited in the deed
Recording the deedOcean County Clerk, Toms RiverMain office at 118 Washington Street

Because the inspection runs through the township's portal, starting it early keeps the closing date from slipping. If the inspector cites a problem, the repair and a second visit have to happen before the certificate issues.

New Jersey puts the realty transfer fee on the seller, collected at recording and based on the price in the deed. The fee schedule gives partial relief to sellers who are qualifying senior citizens aged 62 or older, blind persons, or disabled persons, which matters in a township where so many owners are over 65. A seller claiming the reduction files an Affidavit of Consideration for Use by Seller, which must be notarized and recorded with the deed. Sales above $350,000 use a higher rate table, and a graduated percent fee applies only above $1,000,000.

Buyers weigh the drive more than anything else, since no limited-access highway crosses the township. Route 70 runs through the heart of the township and Route 37 through the east, with County Routes 530, 539, 547 and 571 also in use. The nearest Garden State Parkway entrances are in Toms River, Berkeley and Lacey, and Interstate 195 is reached through Jackson Township. Ocean Ride local bus service runs the OC1 Whiting, OC1A Whiting Express and OC2 Manchester routes. The average commute is 33.3 minutes.

sections.h2: Getting the house ready for the inspector
sections.html:
Walk through the house a few weeks before you apply, with the inspection list in hand. Test each GFCI outlet, replace any smoke detector past its age limit, check that detectors sit clear of vents, and make sure no electrical box is missing its cover. Pull back mulch from decks and porches, put up house numbers that can be read from the street, and confirm that gas, water and electric are on for the visit.

If the house is vacant, leave a lockbox or combination in the application notes so the inspector can get in. Owners who live out of town often forget this step, and a missed visit pushes the closing date. Close any open permits before you apply, because unpermitted work gets cited as a violation and holds up the certificate.

An owner can hire an agent, go it alone, or take an offer from a cash buyer that takes the house without repairs. Each route needs the same township certificate and the same state forms, so the difference comes down to timing and cost.

  • Hiring an agent usually reaches the widest pool of buyers, at the cost of a commission, and the house often needs repairs to pass inspection and satisfy a buyer's lender.
  • Going without an agent saves the commission, though the owner handles pricing, showings, the contract and the paperwork alone.
  • Selling for cash without repairs removes the lender from the picture, which suits inherited, vacant or tenant-occupied houses. Settle in the contract who obtains the re-occupancy certificate and who pays for any repairs it requires.

Whichever route fits, get offers from more than one buyer or agent and compare the net proceeds after the transfer fee, any mortgage payoff and unpaid township charges.

faqs.q: Does Manchester Township require an inspection before I sell?
faqs.a: Yes. The township issues a Certificate of Re-occupancy for resales after an inspection, and the application goes through its online citizen portal. Open permits must be closed first, and wells need an Ocean County Health Department water analysis.

faqs.q: Who pays the realty transfer fee on a Manchester Township sale?
faqs.a: The seller does, at the recording counter. Qualifying seniors aged 62 and older can claim a reduced rate by filing an Affidavit of Consideration.

faqs.q: Where is the deed recorded for a Manchester Township house?
faqs.a: The Ocean County Clerk records deeds, and its main office is at 118 Washington Street in Toms River. The seller's residency form (GIT/REP) goes in with the deed, and the clerk can reject paperwork that is incomplete.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Manchester Township house that needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes, though the re-occupancy inspection still applies. A cash buyer will often accept the condition, but the contract should say who fixes anything the inspector cites and who pays for it before the certificate is issued.

faqs.q: Do mulch and secondary power labels really matter at inspection?
faqs.a: They can. The checklist calls for a label near the electric panel for solar, generators or battery storage, and the state fire code has required 18 inches between mulch and combustible building parts since April 15, 2025. Fixing both ahead of time avoids a failed visit.
